In Roman Law, familia referred to a legal concept of a household consisting of a group of people who were under the authority of the same head of household or paterfamilias. The term familia encompassed not only the immediate family members such as the wife, children, and domestic help, but also extended relatives, clients, and dependents who lived under the same roof and were subject to the power of the paterfamilias. Under Roman Law, the paterfamilias had extensive powers over the members of the familia, including the power of life and death, the right to arrange marriages, and the authority to dispose of property. The concept of familia was central to Roman law and society, as it formed the basis of the Roman social and legal structure, and played a key role in the transmission of property, status, and obligations from one generation to the next.
